nodes.label: Four Revenue Streams
nodes.rationale: Episode -> Premiere -> Premium -> Stars. The client's intent is not to tie users to one subscription but to let them pick a convenient level; this closes open question #1 (subscription vs per-item) with 'both, plus an intermediate level'. The 13.08.2026 client message overrides conflicting TZ figures.

nodes.label: Single Episode Purchase (3 000 UZS)
nodes.rationale: Price lowered from the TZ's 5 000 to 3 000; the V4 mockups and all four PDFs still show 5 000 and are outdated. Only the selected episode unlocks.

nodes.label: Premiere Purchase (15 000 UZS)
nodes.rationale: A new tier absent from the TZ, giving access to all episodes of one series/premiere. The client's wording says 'existing episodes'; whether it covers episodes released later is an open question.

nodes.label: UzCasting Premium Subscription
nodes.rationale: 1/3/6/12 months at 24 000 / 49 999 / 99 000 / 159 900 UZS, the yearly plan flagged as the best value. 'Ad-free viewing' implies non-Premium users see ads — an entire advertising subsystem the TZ never mentions.

nodes.label: UzCasting Stars Donations
nodes.rationale: Internal virtual currency in packs of 10/50/100/500/1000, shown on the creator profile. A second client message extends it to films, a leaderboard, and a monthly awards ceremony — making Stars a ranking mechanic, not just donations, and an entirely new subsystem with no TZ coverage. The Stars-to-UZS rate is still unspecified.

nodes.label: Single Backend Entitlement Check
nodes.rationale: With four possible entitlement sources (episode purchase, premiere purchase, active subscription, free content) the 'can this be watched' check must live in one place on the backend and not be smeared across the client. Requires entities Purchase, Subscription, Entitlement, StarsBalance, StarsTransaction, StarsLeaderboard.

nodes.label: Store Billing Compliance Risk
nodes.rationale: Episodes, premiere access, subscription and Stars are all in-app digital content, which Google Play and Apple require to be sold through their billing at 15-30% commission; Click/Payme/Uzum/UZCARD for such goods violates store rules and gets the app pulled. The commission is taken before the 50/50 creator split (a 3 000 UZS episode yields the creator ~1 050-1 275, not 1 500), Stars are the most tightly regulated category, and the common workaround is selling only on the website with no purchase buttons in the app.
